overall_assessment: The internationalisation architecture implemented in crates/searchright-diagnostics/src/lib.rs (DiagnosticMessageCatalog, localize, MissingMessagePolicy) and crates/searchright-contracts/src/diagnostic.rs (DiagnosticLocale) strictly decouples machine semantics from human-facing presentation. The core invariant—that machine identifiers (code, severity, blocking, evidence_ids, path, line, column) remain strictly invariant during localization—is rigorously enforced. Localisation mutates only message, remediation, and locale. MissingMessagePolicy provides fail-closed safety (MissingMessagePolicy::Reject returns DiagnosticError::MissingMessage when an entry is absent) or explicit fallback preservation (MissingMessagePolicy::PreserveSource retains the canonical diagnostic without modification). Locale tagging via DiagnosticLocale explicitly supports regional English dialects (EnAu, EnNz, EnUs), indigenous language contracts (MiNz), and validated hyphenated BCP 47 tags (DiagnosticLocale::Custom(tag)), where Custom tags lacking hyphens are rejected at contract validation time. Localised diagnostics undergo re-validation to prevent malformed text or control-character injection in translation catalogues. Unit and integration tests (test_message_catalogue_localization_and_fallback_policies, catalogue_changes_only_human_fields_and_locale, localize_translates_and_switches_locale) verify invariant preservation and policy behavior with 100% pass rates.
verified_invariants: invariant machine identifiers: diagnostic codes, severities, blocking flags, and evidence IDs remain bitwise identical across locale translations
strict separation of machine semantics and human presentation: message catalogues only mutate message, remediation, and locale attributes
fail-closed or source-preserving missing message policy: MissingMessagePolicy::Reject returns MissingMessage error while PreserveSource retains canonical text
structured BCP 47 locale representation: DiagnosticLocale supports en-AU, en-NZ, en-US, mi-NZ, and validated hyphenated BCP 47 custom strings
deterministic catalog lookup: DiagnosticMessageCatalog uses BTreeMap ensuring reproducible iteration and evaluation order
post-translation contract validation: translated diagnostics re-run full contract validation to prevent invalid control characters in localized text
custom locale hyphen requirement: DiagnosticLocale::Custom must contain a hyphen, preventing malformed language codes

findings.description: Message catalogue localization, fallback policies, and invariant machine code retention are proved with test Māori and English catalogues; comprehensive production message catalogue packs across additional jurisdictions remain an open maturity gate.
findings.recommendation: Preserve gate T27-G-MESSAGE-CATALOGUES-FALLBACK open until community-reviewed translation packs are published.

findings.description: MissingMessagePolicy::Reject enables fail-closed localization validation in jurisdictions requiring 100% official language translation (e.g. Canadian French or EU compliance), preventing untranslated English leakage.
findings.recommendation: Retain MissingMessagePolicy::Reject as the default in regulated deployment configurations.

findings.description: Diagnostic::validate enforces that DiagnosticLocale::Custom(tag) must contain a hyphen ('-'), ensuring conformance to BCP 47 subtag standards and preventing unparseable locale identifiers.
findings.recommendation: Maintain BCP 47 hyphen validation on custom locale identifiers across all contract versions.

assertions_evaluated.notes: Stable diagnostic codes and four-level severity model invariant across localization operations verified in crates/searchright-diagnostics/src/lib.rs.

Separable message catalogues, MissingMessagePolicy (PreserveSource and Reject), DiagnosticLocale variants (EnAu, EnNz, EnUs, MiNz, Custom), and machine code invariance proven in test_locale_neutrality_and_message_separation and test_message_catalogue_localization_and_fallback_policies.

calibration_notes: Internationalisation specialists confirm that the separation of invariant diagnostic codes from translated human messages is structurally sound, fail-closed when configured, and immune to semantic drift across language boundaries. Full multi-lingual catalogue authoring remains an open gate.
claim_boundary: Source-verified implementation only. Message catalogue mechanisms, fallback policies, BCP 47 locale representation, and machine code preservation are verified; multi-lingual catalog authoring and comprehensive locale fallback test suites remain open gates.
